section.p: Mara reached the lighthouse at dusk. Rain glittered on her dark wool coat, and the copper lantern in her hand threw a small circle of warmth across the worn stone steps. Above her, the tower rose into a sky the colour of old pewter.
At the open door stood an elderly keeper with a silver beard and a crooked brass walking stick. A black cat sat beside his boots. Neither of them looked surprised to see her.

The keeper stepped aside. Inside, a spiral staircase curled around a shaft of darkness, and hundreds of unlit lanterns hung from hooks along the walls. On a table beneath the stairs lay an unfolded chart of an island that Mara had never seen.
She placed her lantern beside the chart. As its light touched the paper, a tiny golden harbour appeared between the inked cliffs. On its smallest pier, a painted boat began to move.

title.p: Chapter II / A Harbour in the Glass

section.p: By morning the rain had stopped. Mara and the keeper climbed to the lamp room, where a great glass lens faced the sea. A pale line of sunlight lay across the wooden floor.

Beyond the lens, an island floated just above the horizon. Its cliffs shone white, and its harbour was crowded with narrow ships whose sails hung motionless in the wind. Mara held the copper lantern close to her chest.

The keeper opened a small hatch beneath the lens. Inside was a shelf with room for one lantern. He pointed to the shelf with his brass stick, and Mara understood why every other light in the tower was dark.
She set the copper lantern into the hatch. The lens filled with amber light. Far away, every window along the island's harbour opened at once, like a hundred eyes waking from sleep.

A narrow boat waited beneath the lighthouse steps. Its hull was painted deep green, and a folded grey blanket lay on its only seat. The black cat leapt aboard before Mara could lift her foot from the last stone.

She looked back. The old keeper stood above her, one hand resting on the brass stick. Behind him the lighthouse windows were warm with copper light, although the morning sun had disappeared behind a bank of cloud.
Mara took the oars. With the first stroke, the sea became perfectly still. The tower and its reflection formed a single column of light behind the boat.
Ahead, the white cliffs grew larger. A figure on the smallest pier raised a lantern in greeting. Mara rowed towards it, while the cat watched the approaching shore with quiet, unmistakable approval.
